final_narrative:
The RaMP enrichment analysis reveals a dominant signal centred on **galactose metabolism and galactosemia**, with five metabolites — galactitol, myo-inositol, sucrose, galactinol, and glycerol — achieving near-perfect enrichment (fold > 870, FDR ≈ 0) in both the KEGG Galactose Metabolism pathway (map00052) and the SMPDB Galactosemia module (SMP00182).

Within the galactose metabolism network, **galactitol (C01697)** is the hallmark driver: it is the terminal polyol that accumulates when galactose cannot be further metabolised, and it is confirmed as a member of Galactose Metabolism and Galactosemia pathways. **Galactinol (C01235)** and **myo-inositol (C00137)** are likewise confirmed members of these same pathways, connected in the reaction graph via a one-hop bidirectional edge (myo-inositol ↔ galactinol). Tracing upstream, sucrose (C00089) feeds into the pathway through glucose and galactose en route to myo-inositol and galactinol (path length 4, forward direction), identifying sucrose as a plausible upstream trigger of the observed accumulation pattern.

The biological picture is consistent with **galactose metabolism dysfunction** reflected in Galactose Metabolism (KEGG map00052) and Galactosemia (SMP00182). Elevated galactitol reflects reduced aldehyde detoxification capacity, a hallmark of classic galactosemia. Glycerol is also a confirmed member of these same pathways (co-occurrence plausibility = 1.0), reinforcing the centrality of galactose metabolism disruption. The convergence of five high-confidence pathway members on this hub makes galactose metabolism the primary affected system.

**Limitations:** Choline and O-phosphoethanolamine could not be verified as members of Galactose Metabolism or Galactosemia via the available pathway-membership data. Their potential contribution remains unconfirmed and warrants targeted follow-up.
